text: Every electric train is a chain. Pull it apart, and you can see every link.
Up top, the catenary. Between New Haven and Boston, it carries twenty-five thousand volts.
A spring-loaded pantograph presses against the wire and pulls that power down.
Inside, a transformer steps it down, and a traction converter reshapes it for the motors.
The motors drive the axles through gears.
Now the clever part. The wheels aren't flat. They're cones.
On a curve, the wheelset slides outward, so the outer wheel rolls on a bigger diameter. The train steers itself.
And when it brakes, the motors become generators, sending energy back.
Above all of it, positive train control. GPS, radio, and onboard computers that can stop the train on their own.
Required by law since two thousand eight. Live on every mandated line by the end of twenty twenty.
Wire. Wheel. Signal. That's a train.
